data.title: Brazil Senate approves fiscal package as government seeks to calm markets
data.description:
By Marcela Ayres

Brazil's Senate approved on Wednesday a a fiscal package that the government sees as essential to meet its fiscal targets and investors view as only a first step toward addressing the country's worsening debt outlook.

Backed by recently reelected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the bill combines spending restraints and revenue-raising measures expected to improve public finances by up to 60 billion reais ($10.29 billion) in 2027.

The package, which now heads to the lower house of Congress, was approved as Finance Minister Dario Durigan sought to reassure markets shaken by mounting fiscal concerns, pledging further action to strengthen public finances.

"We are going to adopt new and additional measures right away," Durigan said on Wednesday, while ruling out changes to Brazil's 3% inflation target or any form of capital controls.

His remarks came amid renewed pressure on Brazil's real , which settled down 1.5% against the US dollar on Wednesday as markets also weighed expectations of higher US interest rates.

The Brazilian currency has weakened about 15% since leftist Lula's surprise election win against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in late October.

Lula's economic team sees the fiscal package as critical to achieving next year's primary surplus target of 0.5% of gross domestic product, while creating room for spending pledges made during the president's campaign, including expanded welfare benefits and support for students.

MARKETS UNDER PRESSURE

Long-dated bond yields climbed and stocks fell on Wednesday, suggesting investors remain unconvinced that Lula — who has yet to name a finance minister for his next term beginning in January — is prepared to pursue deeper spending reforms.

Many economists see such reforms as necessary to stabilize gross debt, which has risen more than 11 percentage points during Lula's current 2023-2027 term to 82.9% of GDP.

The Senate vote also highlighted political hurdles facing the government before it confronts an even more conservative Congress set to take office in February.

Although the package was seen as modest by most analysts, its approval was delayed after the administration did not secure enough support for a Senate vote on Tuesday.

The measure passed only after the government abandoned plans to retain a larger share of transfers owed to states over the coming years. Analysts, however, said that the concession does not change the bill's core objective.

The bill allows additional budget freezes when needed to meet fiscal goals, activating a cap on annual real spending growth of 2%, below the 2.5% ceiling allowed under the current fiscal framework.

It also cuts tax breaks and creates a mechanism to restrict the use of tax credits, boosting revenue.

DETERIORATING DEBT SCENARIO

Economists have welcomed the proposal as a step in the right direction, but many argue it falls short of addressing Brazil's core fiscal challenge: the relentless expansion of mandatory spending.

Next year, the country's budget is set to leave only 8% of expenditures under discretionary control.

BTG Pactual economist Tiago Berriel, a former central bank director, said in a note the bill improves the 2027 primary balance by about 0.2 percentage points of GDP, but does little to alter Brazil's debt trajectory.

The bank estimates gross public debt would now rise to 118% of GDP by 2034, versus 121% without the measure, arguing that public debt would only stabilize by 2030 if annual expenditure growth were limited to 1%.

($1 = 5.8309 reais)

data.title: Montfort Capital Announces Financial Results for the First and Second Quarters of 2026
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Montfort Capital Corp.  ("Montfort" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026 and second quarter ended June 30, 2026. All figures are reported in Canadian dollars unless otherwise noted.

"The first and second quarter results continue to illustrate the trajectory of our financial performance, driven by growth in the loan portfolios of Langhaus and Nuvo and ongoing careful management of expenses," said Ken Thomson, CEO of Montfort. "We are now generating consistent positive cash flow from operations that is sufficient to support our substantially reduced overhead and reinvest in our lending portfolios. I would like to extend my sincere gratitude to our operating team, board of directors and financial partners whose effort and commitment has been fundamental to achieving these significantly improved results."

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

For the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 the Company reports the following highlights:

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $0.5 million or 75% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.0 million increase in interest income on a larger loan portfolio, partially offset by a $0.6 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.2 million or 16% compared to the prior year, mainly due to lower administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.1 million) and amortization ($0.1 million), partially offset by a $0.1 million increase in accounting and legal fees.

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $5.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $0.6 million in the prior year, an improvement of $0.7 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $6.1 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million (sold April 2, 2025).

Six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $1.1 million or 101% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.8 million increase in interest income from loan growth in Langhaus and Nuvo, partially offset by a $1.0 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.9 million or 32% compared to the prior year, primarily due to reductions in administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.3 million), amortization ($0.2 million), bad debts ($0.2 million) and share-based payments ($0.1 million).

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $0.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $1.8 million in the prior year, an improvement of $1.8 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $2.4 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million, partially offset by operating losses of Brightpath and Pivot, including expected credit losses of $5.7 million.

  • Loans receivable as at June 30, 2026, net of allowance, increased by $27.6 million or 13% compared to the balance at December 31, 2025, driven by loan growth in Langhaus ($18.2 million) and Nuvo ($9.4 million). Advances of $58.3 million were partially offset by settlements of $30.6 million.

This news release is qualified in its entirety by the Company's financial statements for the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and the associated Management's Discussion & Analysis, which can be downloaded from the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at https://www.sedarplus.ca/

About Montfort Capital Corp.

Montfort builds and manages private credit portfolios that have focused investing strategies for the institutional and accredited investors markets. For further information, please visit www.montfortcapital.com.

The Company originates, underwrites and manages secured loans through the following operating divisions:

Continuing Operations

Langhaus provides insurance policy-backed lending solutions to high-net-worth individuals and entrepreneurs in Canada. Langhaus' loans are collateralized by the assignment of the borrower's whole life insurance policy, personal and/or corporate guarantees and, in some cases, other tangible collateral.

Nuvo partners with Canadian alternative asset managers and ultra high-net-worth individuals to provide revolving net asset value based loans (ie. 'NAV loans').

Discontinued Operations

The Brightpath business was sold on April 2, 2025. Brightpath is a registered mortgage brokerage and mortgage administrator, administering a portfolio of mortgages secured by residential properties. As at December 31, 2024, the assets and liabilities of Brightpath were classified as held for sale and the operating results are included under discontinued operations up to the date of sale.

The Pivot business was sold on November 4, 2025. Pivot specializes in asset-based lending targeting SME borrowers in Canada. Sources of revenue include net interest income from loans receivable, origination fees and amendment fees. In addition, Pivot earns loan servicing fees and performance fee income for loan management services performed.

For more information, please contact:

data.title: Nvidia's booming demand is 'hard to ignore,' but these four questions loom over the stock
data.description:
By Nora Redmond and Hannah Pedone

Nvidia investors face uncertainty around CEO succession, the AI ecosystem, export controls and China

Nvidia shares rose 3% early Wednesday.

In terms of its numbers, Nvidia took a confident tone with Wall Street on Tuesday. But analysts say a lack of answers to some bigger questions could keep the stock in check for the foreseeable future.

Nvidia's (NVDA) earnings call offered "as much as could be expected under the circumstances" to address concerns associated with the CEO transition, TD Cowen analyst Joshua Buchalter wrote in a note. The topic of future leadership is a source of "immense" uncertainty following the resignation of Jensen Huang a week ago.

Shares of Nvidia surrendered early gains to trade fractionally lower in Wednesday morning action.

Analysts harbor concerns over what the company will look like without Huang. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said he and his team "remain more in the camp that Jensen's removal is going to be problematic, and unfortunately not nearly enough time has passed yet to confirm or disprove those fears."

A second lingering issue for investors is the durability of Nvidia's supplier relationships in the artificial-intelligence ecosystem.

Nvidia's growth trajectory remains closely tied to spending from leading AI labs, which remains "largely outside" the company's control, said Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis. While he believes Nvidia's "demand is hard to argue with," he wrote in a Tuesday note that investors will be looking for strength in the AI ecosystem that would be needed to quell uncertainty over the company's outlook moving forward.

The company acts as a chip supplier for OpenAI and Anthropic as well as an investor with massive equity stakes in both companies.

The matter of China-linked sales leads to two more unresolved questions for Nvidia investors, according to analysts.

One is the issue of whether Nvidia products are making it into China via intermediaries and in violation of export rules on advanced chips. Nvidia "did nothing to assuage growing concerns about its sales to Asian data centers providing service to [Chinese] AI labs," Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg wrote in a note.

He added that Nvidia "stated that they did not forecast any Hopper revenue from [China], which is overly specific and avoids the larger question." Hopper is an older line of Nvidia chips.

A related uncertainty concerns newly implemented rules from the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which put the company's business under "additional scrutiny," Buchalter at TD Cowen wrote.

On Monday, the BIS issued an interim final rule to prevent Chinese companies from tapping into AI chips through "remote access," a practice by which countries like China can make use of U.S. advanced chips via data centers in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.

Buchalter noted that Nvidia's management indicated confidence that the company can reallocate supply to other customers unaffected by the rule.

But Wolfe Research's Chris Caso noted that he has "decided not to follow management" in raising the forecast for next year, given that it's too soon "to fully ascertain the impact of both the export controls, as well as uncertainty regarding the departure of a high-profile CEO."

As for what the uncertainty means for the stock, J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur warned in a Wednesday note that it will likely remain volatile in the near term.

-Nora Redmond -Hannah Pedone

data.description:
(In $000's of Canadian dollars except for shares and per share amounts)

Edmonton, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Titan Logix Corp., ("Titan" or the "Company"), a technology company specializing in mobile liquid measurement solutions, announces its annual results for the three- and twelve-month periods ended August 31, 2026.

"We are gaining traction in the refined petroleum market with the TrueFill PRO product line," said Nick Forbes, CEO at Titan Logix Corp. "The company is focused on growing in this market segment with a completely refreshed product line for fiscal 2027".

Revenues from the Refined Petroleum market for fiscal 2026 totaled $665, or about 10% of total revenue, from new tank truck builds. The Company launched a new website with branded product lines to provide clear, differentiated offerings for each market segment, supporting our sales and marketing efforts with our OEM and dealer network. We expect fiscal 2027 to be a growth year in this segment as we continue to roll out the TrueFill PRO product line to the truck builders.

Q4 marked another key milestone in our strategic plan as the Company received its certification for the TD200, completing the TrueFill PRO product line for the refined petroleum market. The TD200 is a significant improvement over the TD100 that can be reliably manufactured at scale to improve quality and drive down production costs. It has been certified intrinsically safe for use in North America and is designed to meet the certification standards for global markets, positioning the Company for future growth opportunities beyond North America. The Company expects to launch the TD200 in the second fiscal quarter.

FISCAL 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

  • Revenue: decreased slightly by $146 or 2% to $6,608 due to volume compared to $6,754 in fiscal 2025.
  • Gross Profit: decreased by $266 to $3,357 or 51% of revenue in fiscal 2026 compared to $3,623 or 54% in fiscal 2025, driven by planned inventory write-downs attributable to legacy products that the Company no longer actively sells or supports and lower overhead absorption.
  • SG&A excluding stock-based compensation(1): increased by $301 or 11% to $2,970, compared to $2,669 in fiscal 2025, reflecting increased fixed costs to support new product launches and market penetration efforts.
  • Engineering operating expenses: increased by $292 to $398 in Fiscal 2026 when compared to $106 in fiscal 2025, reflecting the absorption of salary costs previously included in Product research and development expenses as key development projects reached completion.
  • Operating EBITDA(1): decreased by $854 to $75 compared to $929 in fiscal 2025, driven by lower gross profit, higher selling, general and administrative and Engineering operating expenses.
  • Total product research and development expenditures(1): decreased by $912 to $1,132 in fiscal 2026 compared to $2,044 in fiscal 2025. The expenses incurred support the Company's diversification and growth into new markets. The reduction is driven by the completion of key development projects resulting in increased expenses being allocated to Engineering operating expenses, lower overall expenses and the impact of realizing $187 of non-refundable federal SR&ED investment tax credits and Alberta Innovation Employment Grant assistance, relating to the 2024 fiscal year.
  • Adjusted EBITDA(1): for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 includes $187 of federal SR&ED investment tax credits and Alberta Innovation Employment Grant assistance relating to the 2024 fiscal year, recorded as a reduction of Product research and development expenses. Excluding this amount, Adjusted EBITDA(1) for the fourth quarter would have been a loss of $100.
  • Loss and comprehensive loss: increased by $175 to a loss of $611 in fiscal 2026 compared to a loss of $436 in fiscal 2025. Net earnings for the fourth quarter also include a deferred income tax recovery of $87.
  • Loss per share (basic and diluted): The Company reported basic and diluted loss per share of $0.02 per share in fiscal 2026 which is consistent with the loss per share posted in fiscal 2025.
  • NCIB update: commencing on May 26, 2026, the Company is authorized to repurchase up to 1,571,185 common shares. As of August 31, 2026, the Company had repurchased 5,000 shares which were held in treasury at that date. Subsequent to August 31, 2026, the Company has repurchased an additional 349,500 common shares of which 25,500 are currently held in treasury.

data.description:
Jan Barta and Dusan Senkypl Disclose TripAdvisor Investment with 7.4% Stake

Jan Barta and Dusan Senkypl, who control Pale Fire Capital, disclosed an investment group’s 7.4% stake in TripAdvisor, Inc., held through Pale Fire Capital SICAV a.s. On Nov. 18, 2026, they reported owning 8,760,345 shares, purchased for about $65.7 million. They said they bought the shares because they believed TripAdvisor was undervalued and offered an attractive investment opportunity.

Investor Intent

Barta and Senkypl say they have no current plan to pursue a specific change at TripAdvisor. They will keep reviewing the investment and may talk with company leaders or shareholders, or propose changes to TripAdvisor’s board, finances or operations. They also may buy or sell shares, but they have not committed to any of those steps.

Investor's Background

Pale Fire Capital and its investment fund, Pale Fire Capital SICAV a.s., invest in securities. Pale Fire Capital investicni spolecnost a.s. manages the fund and acts as its investment manager. Barta and Senkypl control Pale Fire Capital, with Senkypl as board chairman and Barta as supervisory board chairman.

data.title: Kashkari: Markets Expect More Hikes Than Fed Forecasts — Market Talk
data.description: Financial markets seem to be expecting more interest rate hikes ahead than the Federal Reserve's latest forecasts do, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari says at a conference in Washington. The Fed's latest Summary of Economic Projections currently anticipates just one quarter-point hike by the end of 2027, while markets seem to be betting on four. "This is one of the biggest disconnects between what policymakers have been saying and what financial markets are pricing in," Kashkari says. Markets clearly believes the Fed will succeed in bringing inflation down to 2% over the next decade, but will need to be more aggressive than its current posture to do so, he says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: Australia's Challenger says revised Daiichi Life takeover offer falls short
data.description:
Challenger said on Thursday it had rejected a revised takeover proposal from a unit of Japanese insurer Daiichi Life , valuing the Australian investment manager at A$8.17 billion ($5.48 billion).

The revised bid for the remaining 79.5% of shares Daiichi Life does not already own in Challenger is A$12.20 per share, a 2.1% premium to the stock's last close and above Daiichi's earlier offer of A$11.80.

Challenger's board said the revised offer from Daiichi Life does not "adequately represent fair value" for shareholders in the context of a control transaction.

TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty owns a 20.47 % stake in Challenger, according to LSEG data. Daiichi Life, through the unit, had initially acquired a 15.1% minority stake in Challenger from MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings in April 2025.

Daiichi Life did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

($1 = 1.4896 Australian dollars)

data.title: Beam Global Q3 Revenue Rises 15% to $6.7 Million; Gross Margin Improves
data.description:
Beam Global reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $6.7 million, up 15% year over year, and gross profit of $1.4 million, compared with a gross loss in the prior-year quarter. Operating loss was $4.5 million and net loss was $4.47 million; non-GAAP net loss per share improved to $0.11 from $0.16. The company also reported higher backlog and progress on international business and its manufacturing relocation.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $6.660 million, up 15% from $5.788 million in Q3 2025. Revenue for the first nine months was $18.350 million, compared with $19.187 million a year earlier.
  • Gross profit was $1.420 million, with a GAAP gross margin of 21.3%, versus a gross loss of $28,000 and a negative 0.5% margin a year earlier. Adjusted non-GAAP gross profit was $2.127 million, with a 31.9% margin.
  • Loss from operations was $4.499 million, compared with $4.872 million in Q3 2025.
  • Net loss was $4.470 million, or $0.20 per share, compared with $4.870 million, or $0.28 per share, a year earlier. Non-GAAP net loss per share was $0.11, versus $0.16.
  • Backlog was $6.9 million at September 30, 2026, up 28% from $5.4 million at June 30, 2026. Cash was $1.614 million, up from $969,000 at December 31, 2025.

Business Highlights

  • Beam Europe recorded a quarter for smart city infrastructure orders across Serbia, Montenegro, Croatia, Romania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Greece, including infrastructure for Lidl in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
  • The company received more than $500,000 in specialized battery orders from recurring customers in drone and autonomous robotics markets within one week, and presented its high-pulse-power battery design for AI data centers at IECON 2026.
  • Government customers ordered additional EV ARC systems, including the City of Dallas, Dry Creek Rancheria Band of Pomo Indians, and the City of Long Beach. Commercial and community deployments also expanded in Serbia and at four Greater Boston locations through a carsharing pilot.
  • Beam moved its California manufacturing operations to a 55,000-square-foot facility in Yuma, Arizona, and said the relocation is expected to save approximately $3 million in rent over the five-year lease term.
  • Beam introduced its patent-pending BeamHeat product in Ukraine and signed an MOU with Masdar City Free Zone to explore sustainable energy infrastructure opportunities. The company also received a European patent for its Smart Phase Change Composite battery thermal-management technology.
